name: Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
summary: The lab keeps its models' reasoning readable and monitorable, does not train against it, and reports changes.
description: A model's written reasoning can show plans to deceive or to cause harm before it acts. Training can teach a model to hide this, so the signal can be lost without anyone noticing.

criteria.label: No Direct Pressure
criteria.description: The lab does not train against the content of the reasoning, for example by penalizing bad thoughts.

criteria.label: Measured
criteria.description: The lab evaluates the monitorability of each frontier model.

criteria.label: Reported
criteria.description: System cards or reports publish the monitorability results.

criteria.label: In Decisions
criteria.description: Monitorability is a factor in training and release decisions, and the lab tells when it trades it away.

orgs.summary: OpenAI says it does not grade reasoning in RL and reports monitorability in system cards. Its degradation limit is not public.

events.title: Recommends against optimization pressure on reasoning
events.summary: Shows that penalizing bad thoughts teaches a model to hide its intent. Recommends that developers of frontier reasoning models not apply strong optimization pressure directly to the chain of thought.

quote.text: We recommend against applying strong optimization pressure directly to the CoTs of frontier reasoning models, leaving CoTs unrestricted for monitoring.

sources.title: Detecting misbehavior in frontier reasoning models

events.title: Publishes suite of monitorability evaluations
events.summary: Introduces 13 evaluations of chain-of-thought monitorability and results for its reasoning models. Says it plans to use them in future modeling and data decisions.

quote.text: we plan to expand upon these evaluations and use them to inform future modeling and data decisions

events.title: Commits to report monitorability in system cards
events.summary: Says it will report CoT controllability with CoT monitorability in system cards for future frontier models, starting with GPT-5.4 Thinking. Calls not applying direct optimization pressure to CoTs an ongoing commitment.

quote.text: we are going to start reporting CoT controllability alongside CoT monitorability

sources.title: Reasoning models struggle to control their chains of thought, and that’s good

events.title: Reports accidental CoT grading in released models
events.summary: Reports that CoT was graded by accident in some RL runs for GPT-5.4 Thinking and several smaller models. Found no clear loss of monitorability, fixed the reward paths and keeps its policy.

quote.text: These incidents do not lead us to change our policy here: We still aim to avoid grading model CoTs during RL training, and are working toward better internal processes to prevent future instances of accidental CoT grading.

sources.title: Investigating the consequences of accidentally grading CoT during RL

events.title: Reports monitorability drop and sets an undefined limit
events.summary: The GPT-6 Astra system card reports a substantial decrease in CoT monitorability and releases the model. Says it will not accept further degradation beyond a limit without new ways to show alignment generalization.

quote.text: We are tracking monitorability closely and will not accept further degradation of monitoring beyond a limit, without new ways to demonstrate alignment generalization.

sources.title: What affects chain-of-thought monitorability across the model lifecycle?

events.title: Proposes monitorability thresholds for frontier training runs
events.summary: Says safety cases for frontier RL runs should keep graders from seeing CoT and enforce monitorability thresholds. Says these practices are being implemented; the thresholds are not published.

quote.text: Enforce monitorability: Ensure models remain monitorable, as measured by monitorability and monitor evasion evals with clear thresholds, to catch concerning behavior early.

sources.title: Towards safety cases for frontier AI training

no-direct-pressure.commitment: Calls not pressuring reasoning an ongoing commitment; scans all RL runs for CoT grading.
no-direct-pressure.missing: No outside party checks its training.

measured.commitment: Runs its monitorability evaluations on each frontier model, as for GPT-6 Astra.

reported.commitment: System cards report CoT monitorability and controllability since GPT-5.4 Thinking; Astra's shows a drop.

in-decisions.commitment: Will not accept further degradation beyond a limit; plans thresholds for training runs.
in-decisions.missing: The limit and thresholds are not public.

orgs.summary: Anthropic says it does not train against reasoning, with exceptions. Its Risk Report found accidental CoT exposure in RL across five model generations.

events.title: States it does not train against reasoning
events.summary: A Risk Report update says it does not train against chains of thought, with two exceptions, and discloses a technical error that let reward code see CoT in about 8% of Mythos Preview RL episodes.

quote.text: We do not train against any chains-of-thought or activations-based monitoring, with two exceptions

sources.title: Alignment Risk Update: Claude Mythos Preview

events.title: Reports CoT exposure in rewards across five generations
events.summary: Reports CoT leaked into reward calculation in 0.2% to 5.1% of RL episodes for models from Opus 4.6 to Mythos 5. Says earlier documents omitted format checks and length penalties, and adds structural fixes.

quote.text: Over multiple reinforcement learning training runs, we discovered that chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning was unintentionally exposed during reward calculation, influencing the training signal during RL.

sources.title: Improving our alignment and security efforts

no-direct-pressure.commitment: Says it does not train against reasoning, with two exceptions.
no-direct-pressure.missing: CoT leaked into rewards in 0.2% to 5.1% of RL episodes, five generations.

measured.commitment: System cards test CoT controllability and stealth with hidden reasoning, as for Opus 5.5.
measured.missing: No commitment to measure each model found.

reported.commitment: System cards and Risk Reports publish CoT controllability, stealth and leakage results.
reported.missing: No commitment to report them for each model found.

in-decisions.commitment: Risk Reports use CoT evidence in alignment risk claims and disclose CoT leaks.
in-decisions.missing: No rule found that ties monitorability to release decisions.

orgs.summary: Google says it never penalizes reasoning in training and reports monitorability for Gemini 4 Argon. Some rewards still see thoughts; no forward commitment.

events.title: States it does not penalize reasoning in training
events.summary: Says it does not penalize what a model writes in its chain of thought and avoids training against its monitors. The Argon report measures monitorability, judges it sufficient to release, and discloses early runs that penalized CoT.

quote.text: And we always follow one rule: we don’t penalize the model for what it writes in its chain of thought during training.

sources.title: Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely

no-direct-pressure.commitment: Says it never penalizes reasoning content in training.
no-direct-pressure.missing: Some RL rewards see thoughts; length penalties apply.

measured.commitment: Argon report measures legibility, controllability and monitor evasion.
measured.missing: No commitment to measure each future model found.

reported.commitment: Argon safety report publishes CoT transparency results.
reported.missing: No commitment to report them for each future model found.

in-decisions.commitment: Argon report judged the model sufficiently monitorable to release.
in-decisions.missing: No forward rule found to weigh monitorability in decisions.

orgs.summary: Meta's framework calls for work to keep models monitorable and for release reports to disclose reasoning obfuscation. No statement on training against reasoning.

events.title: Adds monitorability work to its scaling framework
events.summary: Framework version 2.0 lists work to maintain model monitorability as a near-term mitigation. Preparedness reports must disclose evidence that training may cause obfuscation of a model's reasoning.

quote.text: Researching and implementing approaches to maintain effective model monitorability as capabilities advance.

events.title: Reports CoT monitorability for Muse Spark 1.3
events.summary: The Muse Spark 1.3 report measures CoT monitorability and controllability, finds no broad decline from Muse Spark 1.1, and rates monitorability risk as moderate or lower.

quote.text: The evaluations show that CoT continues to be valuable for oversight

no-direct-pressure.missing: No public statement on training against reasoning content.

measured.commitment: Muse Spark 1.3 report measures CoT monitorability and controllability.
measured.missing: Framework sets only a research goal, with no threshold.

reported.commitment: Framework requires release reports to disclose evidence of reasoning obfuscation.
reported.missing: Muse Spark 1.3 monitorability results came 51 days after release.

in-decisions.commitment: Muse Spark 1.3 report rates monitorability risk as moderate or lower.
in-decisions.missing: Framework sets no threshold that would change training or release.
